title: Treatment-selection biomarkers for depression
bottleneck: Antidepressant choice is pure trial-and-error: no blood test, scan, or genetic marker reliably predicts which patient responds to SSRIs versus SNRIs versus ketamine versus psychotherapy. Pharmacogenomic panels test drug metabolism, not therapeutic response, and explain little variance in outcomes.
why_it_blocks: Trial-and-error prescribing means months of ineffective treatment, side effects, and dropout before finding something that works, during which depression deepens and suicide risk rises. Precision psychiatry cannot begin without predictive biomarkers.
current_state: EEG, inflammatory markers (CRP), and polygenic scores show weak predictive signals in research. Clinicians use measurement-based care (PHQ-9 tracking) to iterate faster, but selection itself remains unguided. Large consortia are now pooling EEG, MRI, and genomic data to train response-prediction models, but prospective trials proving clinical utility have not yet reported.
